regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY and PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) tell a confident story — until you decompose it. IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY confirms investment is real, not budgeted fiction, and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile) gives the cycle room to run without bottleneck risk. The soft spot is core sector at 4.8% YoY, down from 5.0% — a lagging indicator, but one that historically precedes goods-economy deceleration by two quarters. The quality of this expansion is investment-led, not consumption-led; that makes it durable but also vulnerable to any credit tightening that raises corporate borrowing costs.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83%) is the number RBI publishes; the number that matters is the decomposition. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is benign — 28th percentile — which means the headline overshoot is entirely fuel and food. Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, highest in 10 years) with Brent at $105.6/bbl is the trapdoor: if crude holds above $100/bbl, the RBI's own revised forecast of 5.1% YoY becomes a floor, not a ceiling. The second-order effect is the one consensus is missing: fuel feeds into WPI (already 9.92% YoY), which feeds into manufacturing input costs, which compresses margins before it ever reaches the CPI basket.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits — down 120bps from 82.2% — looks like relief. It is not. Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY is still outpacing deposit growth at 17.8% YoY by 160bps, and the acceleration in credit to industry (20% YoY, up from 6.5%) and services (22.9% YoY, up from 10.2%) means the gap is widening in the segments that matter most for capex funding. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within 12 months, external shocks forced emergency tightening. Today's buffer is larger FX reserves, but the structural tension — credit growing faster than the deposit base that funds it — has not resolved.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. (38th percentile) is the lowest in this cycle, held steady while RBI's own inflation forecast has just been revised up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%. The real rate — repo minus headline CPI — is now effectively zero. That is not a neutral stance; it is an accommodative one being maintained in the face of a 95th-percentile fuel inflation print. The signal for housing affordability is mixed: average home loan rates at 8.15% p.a. have eased, but the affordability index at 10.9× price-to-income is at its worst-ever reading. For corporate capex IRRs, the current rate is supportive — but any hike triggered by fuel passthrough would reprice the entire investment cycle.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY — third consecutive month of acceleration from 16.1% — is the strongest signal in today's data. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) is now above the threshold at which private capex historically accelerates without bottleneck risk. Credit to industry at 20% YoY confirms corporates are borrowing for expansion, not just working capital. The inversion: core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) is the one indicator that does not corroborate the capex story. Core sector — cement, steel, electricity — is the physical substrate of investment. If it is decelerating while IIP capital goods accelerates, one of them is wrong about the cycle's momentum.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month (73rd percentile) is a strong print, but the composition matters more than the headline. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY (61st percentile) signal rural and mass-market demand is genuinely recovering — this is the informal economy's proxy, not the formal sector's. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are mid-cycle, not accelerating. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (26th percentile, down from 5.6%) while vehicle loans grow at 18.8% YoY. Urban discretionary spend on big-ticket items is being financed by credit, not income growth. That is a durable consumption signal only as long as credit conditions stay loose.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Narrows But Stress Persists","data_text":"CD ratio fell to 81% credit ÷ deposits (prev: 82.2%) — a 120bps improvement — yet bank credit growth remains elevated at 19.4% YoY (prev: 11.4%) while deposit growth accelerated to 17.8% YoY (prev: 9.9%). The gap has compressed for one month, but credit is still outpacing deposits by 160bps. NBFC credit growth at 15.8% YoY (prev: 10%) signals continued wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (10y: 0% lo) shows NBFCs are tapping capital markets, but this is a sentinel-low percentile reading — data reliability is questionable.","implication":"Overweight private sector banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they're winning the deposit war. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will rise if RBI tightens liquidity. Watch for RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months if credit-deposit divergence re-widens. Reduce exposure to mid-tier lenders dependent on bulk deposits.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile historically — elevated but not crisis-level. The recent 120bps compression is a relief, but the underlying credit-deposit gap of 160bps is still the widest in 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Accelerating Into Q4","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (prev: 16.1%) — third consecutive month of acceleration. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (prev: 75.6%) — now at 74th percentile, signalling room for incremental capex without bottleneck risk. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (prev: 5%) is the only soft spot, but this is a lagging indicator. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (prev: 6.5%) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (prev: 10.2%) confirm corporates are borrowing for expansion. RBI's GDP forecast at 6.7% YoY (up from 6.6%) and FY estimate at 7.7% YoY (80th percentile) validate the capex narrative.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase allocation to project-linked PSU stocks (NTPC, Power Grid, NHAI). Capex-heavy sectors (auto ancillaries, industrial machinery) will see margin expansion as utilisation rises. Avoid defensive plays — the cycle is in early innings. Hedge with long-duration bonds; capex-driven growth may keep RBI on pause longer than consensus expects.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile is the highest in 3 years. Historically, this level has preceded 12-18 months of sustained capex and earnings growth.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 93rd Percentile, Affluent Rotation Underway","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile, rising 2 consecutive months: ₹31,961 → ₹32,297 → ₹32,490). Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile, up from ₹29,329). DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months: ₹8,930 → ₹58,502). However, SIP YoY growth at 10.7% (30th percentile) and NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile, down from ₹3,051) — a red flag for new investor acquisition.","implication":"SIP inflows are strong in absolute terms, but the collapse in NFO collections and slowing YoY growth suggest affluent money is rotating INTO existing SIP schemes, not new retail entry. Equity valuations are pricing in sustained retail flows — any slowdown in SIP growth will trigger a 5-8% correction. Historically, this level has coincided with market peaks (2021, 2024 early). Monitor for reversal signals.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Pause","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (prev: 20.05%, up 290bps) — 95th percentile, the highest in 10 years. Brent crude at $105.6 / bbl (73rd percentile, rising 3 of last 5 months: $104.4 → $104.7 → $103.4 → $105.5 → $106.5 → $105.7). WTI at $96.1 / bbl (80th percentile, rising 3 of last 5). CPI headline at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83%, 52nd percentile) and food inflation at 7.74% YoY (up from 5.97%, 57th percentile) — both accelerating. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78%, 67th percentile). RBI's inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6%) signals discomfort. Repo rate held at 5.25% p.a. (38th percentile) — the lowest in the cycle.","implication":"RBI will likely signal a rate hike in the next 2-3 policy meetings if fuel inflation stays above 20% YoY. This level has historically forced central banks to tighten within 60 days.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Masks GCC Consolidation, Not IT Recovery","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (7th percentile, but rising 3 of last 5: 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 → 4.02 → 13.2 → 14.1). Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (41st percentile, down from 14.74%, recent: 13.2 → 16 → 14.5 → 14.37 → 14.5 → 14.37). Nifty IT index is flat YTD (Nifty 50 at 22,997, 74th percentile, but IT stocks underperforming). Retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (8th percentile, down from 7.5%, recent: 5.7 → 5 → 4 → 4.8 → 5 → 4.8) — strong recovery. However, Nifty 50 earnings growth is 8-10% (consensus), while office absorption is accelerating. This disconnect suggests Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — not traditional IT services — are the marginal office tenant. GCCs are higher-margin, lower-headcount operations. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding real estate; GCCs (captive centres of MNCs) are expanding. This means office RE is decoupling from IT services stock performance.","implication":"Overweight commercial real estate (Embassy REIT at ₹369.92 / unit, down from ₹434.91 — 15% discount to intrinsic value; MindSpace REIT at ₹345.06 / unit, down from ₹495.02 — 30% discount). Underweight traditional IT services stocks — their real estate footprint is shrinking, and GCC expansion won't drive their earnings. The office absorption surge is a REIT tailwind, not an IT services tailwind. This is a 12-18 month structural trade. Falsifiable: if Nifty IT earnings growth accelerates to > 15% YoY in next 2 quarters, GCC thesis is wrong.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 7th percentile is historically low, but the composition shift (GCCs vs. IT services) is the insight. Retail mall vacancy at 8th percentile (lowest in 10 years) signals consumer confidence and e-commerce saturation — a separate bullish signal for physical retail.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Investment Cycle Accelerates — Inflation Threatens to Pull the Handbrake

The facts:

  • GDP at 7.8% YoY (up from 7.4% YoY) with PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) — both accelerating.
  • IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY for a third consecutive month of acceleration; capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile) — room to run without bottleneck risk.
  • But fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) has forced RBI's own inflation forecast up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% — the real repo rate is now effectively zero.
  • Core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) — cement, steel, electricity — is decelerating while IIP capital goods accelerates; one of them is wrong about cycle momentum.

The tension: The investment cycle is the most credible it has been in a decade, but it is being funded by credit growing faster than deposits and sustained by a real rate of zero — both of which are contingent on RBI staying on hold while fuel inflation runs at a 10-year high.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: if it falls below 4.0% YoY for two consecutive months, the capex narrative loses its physical corroboration.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Equities at Peak Percentiles — Bond Markets and BOJ Disagree

The facts:

  • Nikkei 225 at 64,426 (100th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,168 (100th percentile) — both at 10-year highs, both falling today.
  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile) signals re-acceleration; but US GDP SAAR slowed to 2.2% SAAR from 2.5% — surveys and output are diverging.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.19% yield (94th percentile) — bond markets are tightening for the Fed; US CPI at 3.72% YoY rising for three consecutive months removes any near-term cut.
  • But BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile — highest in 10 years) is the underappreciated variable: yen carry unwind at this rate level has historically transmitted to EM equity outflows within 60–90 days.

The tension: DM equity indices are pricing growth re-acceleration at 100th-percentile valuations; bond markets and decelerating nominal GDP are pricing the opposite. BOJ tightening into this divergence is the tail risk that neither equity nor EM credit markets have priced.

Bottom line: If US 10Y yield crosses 5.30% yield again while BOJ holds at 1.25% p.a., the yen carry unwind accelerates — hedge EM duration and INR exposure.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows Hold the Line — NFO Collapse Signals Retail Fatigue at the Margin

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising for two consecutive months — the structural bid is intact.
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) is absorbing FII equity net outflows of -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) almost exactly.
  • But NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile), down from ₹3,051 cr / month — new investor acquisition has effectively stalled.
  • SIP YoY growth at 10.7% YoY (30th percentile) confirms the existing base is sticky but the incremental growth engine is slowing.

The tension: The SIP base is large enough to offset FII outflows today, but NFO collections at a 2nd-percentile low mean the pipeline of new domestic capital is not being replenished — if SIP growth decelerates further, the DII absorption capacity shrinks precisely when FII outflows may intensify.

Bottom line: Watch monthly NFO collections: a second consecutive print below ₹1,000 cr / month signals retail distribution is losing momentum and DII absorption capacity is at risk.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 92nd Percentile, REITs Repriced — GCCs Decouple Office from IT Stocks

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 10 pp vs prior period), with 25% share within premium/luxury; MMR, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad are the primary destinations, supported by remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY).
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: sales 15% YoY, launches 120% YoY, 28 months unsold inventory — supply is running well ahead of absorption.
  • Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter with GCCs at 41% of occupier mix vs IT services at 15% — Embassy REIT at ₹370, Mindspace at ₹345, Brookfield at ₹263 are all down sharply from prior levels despite rising absorption.
  • Bank Nifty at 55,811 (92nd percentile) is making cycle highs while credit card growth falls to 2.3% YoY (26th percentile) — the bank rally is being driven by corporate and industry credit, not consumer lending.

The tension: Office absorption is rising but REITs are being repriced lower — the market has correctly identified that GCC-driven demand is higher-margin but lower-headcount, meaning rent per square foot may not follow absorption volumes. IT services stocks remain flat YTD for the same reason.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until GCC rental premium data confirms rent-per-sqft is rising; overweight banks with high corporate credit exposure over those dependent on unsecured consumer lending.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Crude, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $105.6/bbl — if crude holds above $104/bbl for another month, RBI's 5.1% YoY inflation forecast becomes untenable and the pause breaks. Probability: high.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — yen carry unwind risk is the most underpriced tail; historical precedent shows EM equity outflows within 60–90 days of BOJ tightening at this magnitude. Probability: medium, impact: severe.
  • CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits with credit still outpacing deposits by 160bps — NBFC wholesale funding stress is the transmission mechanism; corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at a sentinel-low 0th percentile. Probability: medium.
  • But NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) signal domestic retail absorption may be approaching its limit — if SIP growth falls below 8% YoY, the DII buffer against FII outflows narrows materially.

The tension: Each of these risks is manageable in isolation; the scenario where crude stays elevated, BOJ continues tightening, and domestic retail flows plateau simultaneously is the one for which no portfolio is currently positioned.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a close above $108/bbl forces a reassessment of RBI's pause and triggers the inflation-policy-INR chain simultaneously.

"}
